title: Anisotropic thermoelectric transport in the Sr2RuO4-Ru eutectic system
authors: Takeru Ito, Shogo Yoshida, Hiroshi Yaguchi, Ryuji Okazaki
abstract: The Sr2RuO4-Ru eutectic system, in which metallic Ru inclusions are embedded in a Sr2RuO4 matrix, exhibits an enhanced superconducting onset temperature of about 3 K, known as the 3-K phase. Here we investigate the in-plane thermoelectric response of this eutectic system in the normal state and find a pronounced anisotropy in the thermopower for thermal gradients applied parallel and perpendicular to the Ru lamellae. To clarify its origin, we combine thermopower measurements with electronic-structure-based transport calculations and finite-element modeling of the local strain distribution generated by the thermal-expansion mismatch between Sr2RuO4 and Ru. The calculations show that uniaxial compression of Sr2RuO4 produces a sizable thermopower anisotropy through modification of the Fermi surfaces. When an idealized spatially inhomogeneous strain field around the Ru lamellae is included, the observed sign and qualitative magnitude of the anisotropy are reproduced more closely than in a simple unstrained two-component model. These results are consistent with a substantial contribution from strain-induced changes in the Sr2RuO4 electronic structure near the interfaces, although contributions from interfacial phase mixing and three-dimensional transport connectivity cannot be excluded.
summary: This work investigates the anisotropic thermoelectric transport in a $	ext{Sr}_2	ext{RuO}_4$-Ru eutectic system. By combining experimental thermopower measurements with sophisticated DFT and FEM simulations, the authors demonstrate that the observed anisotropy is strongly governed by strain gradients arising from the lattice mismatch between the two components. This highlights strain as a critical tuning parameter for the electronic structure and transport properties of correlated oxides.
main_problem: To understand the origin of the enhanced superconducting onset temperature in the $	ext{Sr}_2	ext{RuO}_4$-Ru eutectic system by investigating its anisotropic thermoelectric response in the normal state.
main_result: The pronounced anisotropy in thermopower is attributed to strain-induced modifications of the $	ext{Sr}_2	ext{RuO}_4$ electronic structure near the interfaces, which is best captured by modeling the inhomogeneous strain field from the eutectic structure.
method: The study combines in-plane thermoelectric measurements (thermopower) with advanced computational modeling, including DFT calculations and Finite-Element Modeling (FEM) to simulate local strain distributions.
model_or_system: The physical system is the $	ext{Sr}_2	ext{RuO}_4$-Ru eutectic, where metallic Ru inclusions are embedded in the $	ext{Sr}_2	ext{RuO}_4$ matrix. The analysis models the strain mismatch and its effect on electronic transport coefficients.
key_observables: In-plane thermopower ($S$) measured parallel and perpendicular to the Ru lamellae, and the resulting thermopower anisotropy ($S_{yy}/S_{xx}$).
important_parameters: Temperature (especially near the 3-K phase), strain components ($\varepsilon[100]$, $\varepsilon[010]$), and the geometry/area fraction of the Ru inclusions.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the strain field generated by thermal expansion mismatch is the dominant source of anisotropy, although contributions from phase mixing and 3D connectivity are noted as possible limitations.
figures_summary: Figures show temperature dependence of measured thermopower vs. calculations under uniform strain, and FEM contour plots illustrating the inhomogeneous strain field generated by the Ru inclusions, comparing calculated anisotropy ratios to experiment.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by first presenting experimental measurements of anisotropic thermopower in the eutectic system. It then develops theoretical models, starting with uniform strain calculations, progressing to complex FEM simulations incorporating inhomogeneous strain fields, and finally comparing the resulting anisotropic transport coefficients to the experimental data.
why_interesting: The study links macroscopic transport properties (thermoelectric response) directly to microscopic structural details (interfacial strain) in a correlated material system, providing a strain-sensitive probe for understanding superconducting mechanisms.
